installation.script:
#!/bin/ash
# Leaf Installation Script
# Leaf is a Paper fork; the jar is resolved from Leaf's v2 build API.
#
# Project:   https://www.leafmc.one
# API:       https://api.leafmc.one/v2

PROJECT=leaf
API=https://api.leafmc.one/v2/projects/leaf
USER_AGENT="Pterodactyl (https://pterodactyl.io)"

cd /mnt/server

# A supplied download URL wins, exactly as it does on the Paper egg.
if [ -n "${DL_PATH}" ]; then
    echo "Using supplied download url: ${DL_PATH}"
    DOWNLOAD_URL=`eval echo $(echo ${DL_PATH} | sed -e 's/{{/${/g' -e 's/}}/}/g')`
    curl --fail --user-agent "${USER_AGENT}" -o ${SERVER_JARFILE} ${DOWNLOAD_URL} || {
        echo "Failed to download from the supplied URL."
        exit 1
    }
    exit 0
fi

# The payload is piped with printf, never echo: dash's echo interprets
# backslash escapes, which rewrites the escaped quotes inside the JSON and
# corrupts it into something jq cannot parse.
#
# Leaf's build list contains raw control characters inside commit messages --
# newlines and tabs appear literally inside JSON strings, which is invalid JSON
# and makes jq reject the entire document. Stripping every control character
# (including tab/newline/carriage return) is safe here: those three are only
# ever JSON whitespace *between* tokens, and removing them cannot join two
# tokens together in this payload.
#
# The `tr` is written out inline at every use rather than held in a variable: a
# variable would need the octal escapes in single quotes, and ${VAR} expansion
# does not re-parse them, so tr would receive literal backslashes and silently
# strip nothing.

if [ -z "${LEAF_VERSION}" ] || [ "${LEAF_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
    LEAF_VERSION=$(curl -sSL ${API} | tr -d '\000-\037' | jq -r '.versions[0]')
fi

# Leaf does not publish every version; fall back rather than fail the install.
VER_EXISTS=$(curl -sSL ${API} | tr -d '\000-\037' | jq -r --arg V "${LEAF_VERSION}" '.versions | index($V) != null')
if [ "${VER_EXISTS}" != "true" ]; then
    LEAF_VERSION=$(curl -sSL ${API} | tr -d '\000-\037' | jq -r '.versions[0]')
    echo "Minecraft version not offered by Leaf; using ${LEAF_VERSION}"
fi

# Resolve the build. Newest stable ("default") is preferred; some versions only
# ever publish experimental builds, so fall back to the newest of any channel
# rather than leaving the install with nothing to download.
if [ -z "${LEAF_BUILD}" ] || [ "${LEAF_BUILD}" = "latest" ]; then
    BUILDS=$(curl -sSL "${API}/versions/${LEAF_VERSION}/builds" | tr -d '\000-\037')
    LEAF_BUILD=$(printf '%s' "${BUILDS}" | jq -r '[.builds[] | select(.channel=="default")] | if length > 0 then max_by(.build).build else empty end')
    if [ -z "${LEAF_BUILD}" ] || [ "${LEAF_BUILD}" = "null" ]; then
        echo "No stable Leaf build for ${LEAF_VERSION}; using the newest available."
        LEAF_BUILD=$(printf '%s' "${BUILDS}" | jq -r '[.builds[].build] | max')
    fi
else
    BUILDS=$(curl -sSL "${API}/versions/${LEAF_VERSION}/builds" | tr -d '\000-\037')
    BUILD_EXISTS=$(printf '%s' "${BUILDS}" | jq -r --arg B "${LEAF_BUILD}" '[.builds[] | select((.build|tostring) == $B)] | length > 0')
    if [ "${BUILD_EXISTS}" != "true" ]; then
        echo "Leaf build ${LEAF_BUILD} does not exist for ${LEAF_VERSION}; using the newest stable."
        LEAF_BUILD=$(printf '%s' "${BUILDS}" | jq -r '[.builds[] | select(.channel=="default")] | if length > 0 then max_by(.build).build else ([.builds[].build] | max) end')
    fi
fi

if [ -z "${LEAF_BUILD}" ] || [ "${LEAF_BUILD}" = "null" ]; then
    echo "Could not resolve a Leaf build for ${LEAF_VERSION}."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Version being downloaded"
echo "MC Version: ${LEAF_VERSION}"
echo "Leaf build: ${LEAF_BUILD}"

DOWNLOAD_URL="${API}/versions/${LEAF_VERSION}/builds/${LEAF_BUILD}/downloads/leaf-${LEAF_VERSION}-${LEAF_BUILD}.jar"
echo "Downloading: ${DOWNLOAD_URL}"

# --fail turns an HTTP error into a non-zero exit instead of writing the error
# page to disk as if it were the jar.
curl --fail --user-agent "${USER_AGENT}" -o ${SERVER_JARFILE} ${DOWNLOAD_URL} || {
    echo "Failed to download ${DOWNLOAD_URL}"
    exit 1
}

# A jar is a zip archive, so it must start with "PK". Without this check a
# truncated or error response would be installed and only fail much later, at
# server start, with a far less obvious message.
if [ ! -s "${SERVER_JARFILE}" ] || [ "$(head -c 2 ${SERVER_JARFILE})" != "PK" ]; then
    echo "Downloaded file is not a valid jar; aborting."
    rm -f ${SERVER_JARFILE}
    exit 1
fi

# Paper forks refuse to start without these; the vanilla file is only fetched
# when missing so a reinstall keeps a customised copy.
if [ ! -f server.properties ]; then
    echo "Downloading MC server.properties"
    curl -sSL -o server.properties https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pterodactyl/game-eggs/main/minecraft/java/server.properties
fi

echo "done"
